title: Swiggy Uses 350+ Features and Multi-Task MLP to Predict Customer Lifetime Value
gist: Swiggy built an in-house predicted lifetime value model using 350+ pre-first-order features and a small multi-task MLP that shrank 63% (363,000 to 135,000 parameters) while getting more accurate, and feeds the ranking into Google tROAS ad bidding. In A/B tests its own model beat a third-party pLTV platform on retention and gross order value per acquired user, though the external vendor acquired more users per dollar.

insights.claim: In production A/B experiments, an in-house predicted-lifetime-value model delivered higher retention and gross order value per acquired user than a third-party pLTV platform, without incurring additional platform costs, while the external platform acquired more users per dollar spent.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Volume-optimizing third-party acquisition vendors can look better on CPA while destroying value per user — a direct risk to marketing-tech vendors billing on acquired-user counts.
insights.quote: The company's model delivered higher retention and gross order value per acquired user without additional platform costs, while the external platform acquired more users per dollar spent.
insights.locator: Swiggy also compared the in-house model

insights.claim: Consumer platforms with enough first-party signal can build value-prediction models in house and drop a paid third-party pLTV vendor while improving downstream unit economics.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Insourcing pressure on adtech measurement and LTV-prediction vendors as large consumer apps mature their data teams.
insights.locator: Swiggy also compared the in-house model

insights.claim: Adding a second auxiliary prediction task (order count) alongside lifetime value shrank a model's parameter count by 63%, from 363,000 to 135,000, while marginally improving results.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Multi-task auxiliary heads are a cheap lever for cutting inference cost and model size — relevant wherever serving cost, not accuracy, is the binding constraint.
insights.quote: The twist: adding a second prediction task shrank the model by 63% — and made it more accurate.
insights.locator: Soumyajyoti Banerjee, Staff Data Scientist at Swiggy

insights.claim: A relatively simple multilayer perceptron with three shared hidden layers and task-specific heads was chosen over a more complex architecture for lifetime-value prediction, producing a four-head model across two business lines.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Evidence that production ML value often comes from feature coverage and task design rather than architectural novelty — tempering the case for expensive model complexity.
insights.locator: The model uses a relatively simple multilayer perceptron

insights.claim: The lifetime-value model uses more than 350 features spanning acquisition channel, device and fraud signals, geographic behavior, complaint history, category affinity, order behavior, payment patterns and socioeconomic indicators, all generated from information available before a customer's first order.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Pre-first-order feature breadth is the moat here, not the model — it depends on owning device, fraud and geographic telemetry that pure ad platforms lack.
insights.locator: Swiggy's approach uses more than 350 features

insights.claim: A large share of new users place no orders during their first 30 days while a small group generates substantially higher lifetime value, producing a highly skewed target distribution that the model must resolve between users who initially appear identical.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Extreme value skew in consumer marketplaces means average-CPA optimization systematically misprices the tail — a structural argument for value-based bidding.

insights.claim: The design goal was to produce a useful value signal before a customer's first order so predicted value could drive advertising bid optimization instead of short-term conversion metrics.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: The shift from conversion-optimized to value-optimized bidding changes which ad platforms win budget — those that accept custom value signals gain share.
insights.quote: The problem wasn’t producing a score; it was producing a score that could survive sparse early signals.
insights.locator: Swiggy has developed an in-house predicted lifetime value

insights.claim: Conventional regression metrics such as mean absolute error and mean absolute percentage error were judged insufficient for lifetime-value models because of the large number of zero-value users and the long tail of customer value.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: When evaluating vendor LTV claims, demand rank-quality metrics — headline error rates on skewed targets are close to meaningless.
insights.locator: According to Jayshmi A, an engineer at Swiggy

insights.claim: Evaluation was reframed as a ranking problem: predicted and actual values are split into ten quantiles and the metric is how often users land in the corresponding predicted and actual deciles.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Decile-coverage heatmaps are the practical acceptance test for any value model feeding a bidding system.
insights.locator: Instead, Swiggy evaluated whether the model

insights.claim: The model achieved a Spearman correlation above 0.75 for both the food delivery and quick-commerce business lines, with 70% to 80% diagonal coverage across value deciles.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A concrete benchmark bar for anyone assessing pLTV vendors or internal builds.
insights.locator: The model achieved a Spearman correlation above 0.75

insights.claim: The predicted lifetime value signal is fed into Google's target return on ad spend (tROAS) bidding, with the intended workflow being to rank customers by predicted value and let the ad system differentiate bids on that ranking.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Google captures the value uplift only if advertisers can supply their own value signals — reinforces the strategic importance of first-party conversion-value plumbing.
insights.locator: In production, Swiggy uses the pLTV signal

insights.claim: The next stage of the work moves from point estimates to probabilistic lifetime-value predictions, representing uncertainty in customer value and incorporating that uncertainty into bidding decisions.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Uncertainty-aware bidding is the next frontier in performance marketing; early movers can bid more aggressively on high-variance segments.
